messages:
Maria (sales): hey team, running a POC with AcmeCorp — they say they can see requests in the console but traces aren't showing up in Datadog and logs lack trace IDs. hitting 429s intermittently too :grimacing:
Ajay (solutions): thanks — do we have an example trace id or raw log line from their side? also which export are they using (datadog/splunk/elk)?
Tayler (customer): paste from our app logs: 

2026-03-20T14:03:12Z INFO request received method=POST path=/v1/generate status=429 latency_ms=112 message="rate limited by model" trace_id=null request_id=\"\" 

we're using your datadog-forwarder export configured via console -> Observability -> Log exports
Maria (sales): they also showed an inbound header dump: no traceparent or x-request-id present. just Authorization and content-type.
Frank (obs-eng): ok this is two issues: 1) no trace propagation header so our agent can't attach spans/trace_id 2) export pipeline is emitting logs but missing trace_id field so datadog can't correlate.
Frank (obs-eng): quick checklist: 1) instrument client to forward W3C traceparent (or X-Request-Id) to Redwood API 2) configure log export to include trace_id/json_key 3) confirm no upstream proxy is stripping trace headers
Ajay (solutions): Tayler — can you try sending a test request with traceparent header and paste the response headers? sample curl: 

curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -H 'traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01' \n  -d '{"input":"hello"}'

Tayler (customer): doing it now -> response headers show x-redwood-trace: 4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736
Tayler (customer): updated log: 

2026-03-20T14:11:05Z INFO request received method=POST path=/v1/generate status=200 latency_ms=54 trace_id=4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736 request_id=\"req-9a2\"

so sending traceparent worked. previous client lib didn't propagate W3C headers.
Frank (obs-eng): perfect. next: make sure your app injects traceparent on every outbound call to Redwood. example snippets: 

# python requests
import requests
headers = {
  'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + API_KEY,
  'Content-Type': 'application/json',
  'traceparent': traceparent_value
}
resp = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers)

// node fetch
await fetch(url, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${KEY}`, 'traceparent': tp },
  body: JSON.stringify(payload)
})

Frank (obs-eng): also update your log shipper mapping so that the field is named "trace_id" in the JSON payload. Datadog will auto-link traces if the trace_id is present and in hex format. if you must, set the pipeline rule to copy x-redwood-trace -> trace_id.
Maria (sales): Tayler asked about the 429s — any quick mitigation without changing client?
Frank (obs-eng): short-term: implement exponential backoff + jitter on 429s; long-term: we can spin up a dedicated pool for the POC (reserved capacity) or increase concurrency limits in the project. I can open a temporary burst policy for AcmeCorp if you want.
Maria (sales): please, that would help with demo tonight.
Frank (obs-eng): opened request: #INC-8593 to add temporary burst capacity for project acme-poc until 2026-03-25. observability-bot: New export updated: datadog-forwarder-acme (jsonl) — 2026-03-20T14:15:12Z
Ajay (solutions): TY Frank. one more note — when you configure the drain in console, use newline-delimited JSON, with fields: timestamp, level, message, trace_id, request_id. sample mapping near the bottom of the UI.
Tayler (customer): updated our app to forward traceparent and changed log format — I can now search trace:4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736 in Datadog and see the whole request->response pipeline :party-parrot:
Maria (sales): awesome. I'll confirm with AcmeOps after demo. marking as resolved unless anything else?
Frank (obs-eng): also added a short-runbook to the ticket: how to detect missing propagation (search for trace_id=null or trace_id=""), and how to patch common node/python libs. happy to pair if they need code help.
Maria (sales): thanks everyone :raised_hands:
